html:
SMTO-EXE-0035 — SMTO passed information to a command the wrong way

GUID: cd6666d7-5328-49d0-ae70-fed574b7b1f3
Slug: shell-input-invalid
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO tried to hand some information to a command, but it labeled or attached that information in a way commands can't accept. The command did not run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a moment and watch the task. SMTO normally corrects how it passes the information and tries the step again. This refusal is reported back to SMTO, and the command never started.
  2. If the task stops, ask SMTO in the conversation to run that step again using simple names made of letters, numbers and underscores for its inputs. Commands only accept input names in that simple form.
  3. If the command needs text typed into it, ask SMTO to give that text directly or from one earlier result, not both. SMTO accepts only one way of feeding text into a command at a time.

What success looks like

  • The step runs and its output shows the command used the information you expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the same request unchanged; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Shell request preparation rejected an input or environment name that is not a safe identifier ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*), or a stdin_text/stdin_input_name supplied under a non-matching stdin_mode.

What this means

  • Shell request construction rejected an invalid environment identifier or a stdin value/reference supplied under the wrong stdin mode. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Shell request construction rejected an invalid environment identifier or a stdin value/reference supplied under the wrong stdin mode.

How to diagnose it

  • Check environment-name syntax and pair stdin_text with literal mode or stdin_input_name with input_binding mode.

How to fix it

  • Rename bound inputs and terminal environment variables to safe identifiers (agent_runtime.execution.shell_request.prepare_request, agent_runtime.execution.target_shell.terminal_env_prefix). Pair stdin_text only with stdin_mode=literal and stdin_input_name only with stdin_mode=input_binding (CodeTool.execute), then resubmit the corrected call.
  • Use safe environment identifiers. Pair stdin_text with literal mode and stdin_input_name with input_binding mode.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The shell input mapping validates and supplies the exact intended values through the chosen mode.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
